scenes.heading: Gene structure and expression
scenes.sub: From a gene to a working polypeptide
scenes.say: A gene is only useful if the cell can read it. Gene expression turns the information in a gene into a product, usually a polypeptide. It explains how one base change can cause sickle cell anaemia.

scenes.heading: Parts of a gene
scenes.say: Think of a gene as a bus route. The promoter is the stop where RNA polymerase climbs on. In prokaryotes, the operator is a boom gate where a repressor can block it. The coding region has exons and introns. The terminator is where transcription ends.

scenes.heading: Transcription
steps: DNA unwinds; template strand is read
scenes.say: In transcription, RNA polymerase binds the promoter and unwinds the DNA. It reads the template strand and builds complementary RNA, with U pairing with A. At the terminator, it lets go. In eukaryotes, this first copy is called pre-mRNA.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Cutting the ads out of a recorded footy match
scenes.science: Splicing cuts introns out of pre-mRNA and joins the exons
scenes.breaks: ads are rubbish, but introns aren't always useless, and the cuts happen to the RNA copy, never to the DNA.
scenes.say: Splicing is like cutting the ads out of a recorded footy match. The introns are the ads, cut out by the spliceosome. The exons are the game, joined together. Different highlight reels from one recording means one gene can make several polypeptides. A five prime cap and poly A tail protect the mRNA.
scenes.caption: Splicing is like cutting the ads out of a recorded footy match. The introns are the ads, cut out by the spliceosome. The exons are the game, joined together. Different highlight reels from one recording means one gene can make several polypeptides. A 5′ cap and poly-A tail protect the mRNA.

scenes.heading: Translation
scenes.say: At the ribosome, mRNA is read three bases at a time. It starts at A U G. Each tRNA anticodon matches a codon and brings one amino acid, joined by peptide bonds. At a stop codon, no tRNA matches, so a release factor frees the polypeptide.
scenes.caption: At the ribosome, mRNA is read three bases at a time. It starts at AUG. Each tRNA anticodon matches a codon and brings one amino acid, joined by peptide bonds. At a stop codon, no tRNA matches, so a release factor frees the polypeptide.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: The template strand reads 3′-TAC GGA TTC ACT-5′. Write the mRNA and the amino acids.
lines: Pair the bases: T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C
AUG = Met, CCU = Pro, AAG = Lys
scenes.say: Pair each template base. The mRNA reads A U G, C C U, A A G, U G A. That's methionine, proline, lysine, then a stop codon. Three amino acids.
scenes.caption: Pair each template base. The mRNA reads AUG, CCU, AAG, UGA. That's methionine, proline, lysine, then a stop codon. Three amino acids.

scenes.heading: Don't mix these up

right.title: Stop codon
points: An mRNA codon: UAA, UAG, UGA

scenes.say: Don't confuse the terminator with a stop codon. The terminator is in the DNA and ends transcription. A stop codon is in the mRNA and ends translation.

points: Introns out, exons joined; cap and tail added
Translation: AUG to a stop codon
scenes.say: Quick recap. RNA polymerase transcribes the gene from the promoter to the terminator. Eukaryotes splice out introns and add a cap and tail. Ribosomes translate from the start codon to a stop codon. Now try the practice questions!
